 | 2 | Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)
 | Learners should be able to give accounts of the main events of the Prophet’s life (after the call to
 | prophethood) and his significance in Muslim beliefs. They should show understanding of the importance of
 | the Prophet’s actions and experiences in the history and development of Islam. Learners should know and
 | understand the importance of the example the Prophet (pbuh) provided, as a role model and as a leader,
 | and evaluate what this means for present-day individuals and for communities.

 | 5.2 Articles of Faith and the Five Pillars of Islam
 | Learners should study each of the following beliefs and observances, and their basis from the Qurʾan
 | and Hadith. They should be aware of their significance in the faith and action of individual Muslims,
 | including the benefits and the contribution they make to Muslim communities today.
 | (a) An overview of the Articles of Faith and how they are based on the Qurʾan and sunnah.
 | (b) The following three Articles of Faith should be studied in detail:
 | • the oneness of God (tawhid)
 | • prophethood (risalah)
 | • beliefs about the afterlife (akhirah).
 | (c) The Five Pillars of Islam, including observances and significance for each:
 | • the statement of faith (shahadah)
 | • daily prayer (salah)
 | • alms tax (zakah)
 | • fasting (sawm) in Ramadan
 | • pilgrimage (Hajj) to Makkah.

 | 6.2 Rites of passage
 | (a) Birth and upbringing - the aqiqah ceremony; the importance of family life; learning about Islam
